subject: Quantify hyperscaler perf gap — quick recap & next tests
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@acmehealth.io>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 8 May 2029 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick discovery — perf targets and baseline

Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Wanted to capture the baseline numbers our infra team pulled this morning (attached) and confirm a couple of asks so we can move to a side-by-side run:

- Baseline included p95 ~140ms, p99 ~360ms (avg sequence 320 tokens, small prefix caching).
- We see 18–22 tokens/sec per stream on HyperscalerX with their latest runtime.
- We can provide a short set of 500 representative prompts and an S3 bucket for test harness access.

Two asks from our end: can Redwood run a short A/B (hyperscaler vs Redwood-hosted) with these same workloads, and can you propose a minimal test spec (setup, windows, metrics) so our platform team can approve access?

Also we need confirmation around data retention/persistence for the test logs (we are bounded by HIPAA controls). If you can include a SOC2 reference and the retention policy you'll use for the test logs, that would help.

I attached the baseline export as acme-baseline.csv.

—Liam
Senior Platform PM
Acme Health

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@acmehealth.io>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Quantify hyperscaler perf gap — proposed A/B spec

Liam — great talking yesterday. Quick recap and concrete next steps below so we have alignment before the test kickoff.

Recap:
- Goal: side-by-side latency & throughput A/B comparing HyperscalerX managed endpoint → Redwood hosted runtime and Redwood Dedicated (if useful).
- Primary metrics: p95, p99, median, tokens/sec (per stream), and cost-per-token. Secondary: cold-start variance and KV cache hit-rate.

Proposed minimal A/B test spec (attached as redwood-ab-test-spec.md):
- Test window: 72h continuous run (we suggest May 14–16) with three 4-hour steady-state windows for analysis.
- Workload: 500 representative prompts with sequence lengths sampled from your baseline (avg 320 tokens).
- Concurrency: 32 parallel streams; batch config: dynamic batching disabled for parity (we'll run separate runs with batching ON to show gains).
- Metrics capture: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec per stream, CPU/GPU utilization, request/response size, and request traces for 1% sampled traffic.

What we need from you today:
1) Confirm the test window (May 14–16) or propose alternate dates.
2) Grant read-only test access to the HyperscalerX endpoint or provide request logs with timing for the baseline runs.
3) Confirm data retention constraints (HIPAA note) — our test logs can be auto-purged within 7 days and we can provide a SOC2 report link.

Next steps: once you confirm we'll schedule a 30-min tech kickoff (Jordan will run infra coordination) and share a signed test access form.

Attachment: redwood-ab-test-spec.md (test plan, measurement notes, sample payloads)

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0182

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai

Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@acmehealth.io>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quantify hyperscaler perf gap — infra notes

Looping in a few infra specifics so Liam knows what we'll need on the engineering side:

- We'll run the Redwood-hosted baseline on our latest runtime (attention-optimizations + int8 quantization path) and a Dedicated run if you want to compare pinned capacity.
- Perf harness: our jenkins job will drive the 32 parallel streams; attached is test-harness-config.yaml (connection endpoints, auth token TTLs, sample env).
- Regions: we recommend us-west-2 for latency parity vs your reported numbers; if you prefer another region we can mirror that.
- Tracing: we'll collect spans at request-level; to avoid PHI leaving your boundary we'll take only timing metadata unless you opt-in to payload-level traces.

Operational ask: please provide an IAM principle or the ephemeral service account we should use to pull the sample prompts from S3. We'll rotate keys per test window.

Attachment: test-harness-config.yaml

-Jordan
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@acmehealth.io>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 May 2029 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantify hyperscaler perf gap — proposed A/B spec

Marissa / Jordan — thanks for the clear spec. Quick answers:

- Test window: May 14–16 works for us.
- We will provide a read-only service account for the S3 payloads and an ephemeral HyperscalerX token for the parallel runs (we need a short form from you to OK for security).
- Retention: we require logs to be deleted within 7 calendar days and stored encrypted-at-rest; SOC2 attestation is sufficient (please send link).

Baseline numbers (attached): p95 140ms, p99 360ms, tokens/sec 18–22. Our teams would treat results as successful if p95 < 120ms and tokens/sec >= 25 for parity with internal SLAs; p99 < 300ms is a strong differentiator.

We'll also share a small list of production prompts with personally-identifiable token anonymization.

Attachment: acme-baseline.csv

-Liam
